The six established resources and their pinned releases are preserved.
Custom firmware for the 2DS / 3DS family, including New models. It runs through a persistent exploit such as boot9strap; an archive alone does not install CFW on a stock console.
A full-access file browser for NAND backups, cartridge dumping and system maintenance. Follow its usage guide before making writes to system storage.
Find, install and update homebrew from Universal-DB and other Unistores directly on the console. Includes app search, screenshots and a download queue.
Back up and restore supported game saves and extdata. Use the 3DS CIA on a prepared 2DS / 3DS, and keep an original backup before restoring or editing saves.
Access SD-card files from an FTP client on your local network. This CIA is the 2DS / 3DS build, separate from the Nintendo DS binary.
Launch DS-mode homebrew on a CFW-enabled 2DS / 3DS. Follow the 3DS-specific installation steps; its package differs from the DS flashcard and DSi builds.
Manage HOME Menu themes, boot splashes and badges.

Luma3DS custom firmware; CIA installs to HOME Menu, 3DSX runs through Homebrew Launcher. Theme folders or ZIPs belong in /Themes; splash folders in /Splashes. Open HOME Menu theme settings once first. Region-changed systems must use a functioning HOME Menu/theme extdata for their installed region.
On-console Pokémon save manager and editor with storage banks.

Supported Pokémon save files; back up each save in Checkpoint before editing. It manages saves, it does not supply the games. Internet is used to obtain verified additional assets. See project wiki for exact generation/title/save support.
File manager for browsing and organizing files on the console SD card.

Use stable v5.1.0 rather than the separately published next-v1.00 prerelease. CIA needs custom firmware; 3DSX needs Homebrew Launcher. Keep a PC backup before moving/deleting files, especially Nintendo 3DS and save data.
Read hardware, firmware, battery and system information directly on the handheld.
Runs as CIA on a custom-firmware system or 3DSX in Homebrew Launcher. Useful for identifying the actual Old/New model before choosing model-limited software. No BIOS or game data needed.
Nintendo Homebrew archive of the original FBI title manager release.

Archived FBI 2.6.1 release, not a new fork version. Use on a system already running custom firmware. CIA files are installers; install only software you trust and keep homebrew 3DSX separate from installed titles. Follow 3ds.hacks.guide finalizing setup for initial FBI installation.
Dump the handheld DSP firmware needed by homebrew audio applications.

Creates /3ds/dspfirm.cdc from your own console. Use the DSP1 CIA or 3DSX; DSP2 is an alternative CIA with automatic self-removal and is intentionally not selected here. No downloaded DSP firmware is supplied.
Browse and install actual 3DS/2DS themes, boot splashes and badges from Themezer on the handheld.

Luma3DS custom firmware and a working HOME Menu with Change Theme support. Install the CIA using FBI, or copy the 3DSX to /3ds/ for Homebrew Launcher. Themes use /Themes, splash packages /Splashes and badges /Badges; cache/settings use /3ds/themezer-3ds/. This is the 3DS app, not the Switch NXThemes installer. Region support depends on the installed HOME Menu; do not region-change a console solely to install themes.

Use a genuine SD / microSD with FAT32 and an MBR partition table. The maintained guide recommends 2–128 GB; larger cards can introduce GBA graphics and custom-theme issues. Keep the entire existing Nintendo 3DS folder and your saves backed up.
CIA apps: install to HOME Menu
Copy a CIA to a convenient SD folder such as /cias/, then use FBI on your prepared CFW system to install it. Read the app requirements first. Universal-Updater is another route for supported apps.
Put the executable in /3ds/ or its documented app subfolder. Copy bundled data directories separately to their specified SD paths. A lone 3DSX is not a replacement for required game data.
For tools that document it, put the FIRM under /luma/payloads/ and use the Luma chainloader at boot. Luma boot.firm itself belongs at the SD root; do not replace it with an app FIRM.
Follow TWiLight Menu++’s 3DS installation page. The DS flashcart and DSi packages use different instructions.

Original and New hardware have different performance limits.
New 3DS means New 3DS, New 3DS XL or New 2DS XL. Keep games, BIOS files and saves in the locations required by each project. No commercial ROMs or BIOS files are included here.
Nintendo 64 emulator port with dynamic recompilation and hardware rendering.

New 3DS/New 2DS is the practical target; compatibility and speed vary substantially by game. Extract the release data archive to the SD root; put at least one legally dumped ROM in /3ds/DaedalusX64/Roms/. Use recent Luma and dumped DSP firmware. Remove an older preferences.ini when following the release upgrade instructions.
Snes9x (updated fork) screenshot published by Universal-DB
Updated Snes9x port with save-state previews, scaling, scanlines and compatibility fixes.

Supports original 3DS/2DS and New models; demanding enhancement-chip games can run more slowly on original hardware. Supply legally dumped SNES ROMs. No general SNES BIOS is needed; consult the project known-issues list for Satellaview/BS-X and title-specific exceptions. Current fork uses NDSP audio, so complete DSP setup.
Red Viper screenshot published by Universal-DB
Virtual Boy emulator with stereoscopic 3D, configurable controls and local wireless multiplayer.

Works on original and New 3DS/2DS; 2DS has no stereoscopic display. Requires Luma custom firmware for the dynamic recompiler and DSP firmware for audio. Load legally dumped .vb ROMs (ZIP supported) from any SD folder. Gateway-style flashcarts alone do not meet the runtime requirement.
Game Boy, Game Boy Color and Game Boy Advance software emulator with save states.

New 3DS is recommended for GBA; original 3DS is slower and full speed is game-dependent. Supply legally dumped ROMs; original BIOS dumps are optional for normal HLE operation and needed for BIOS-specific behavior. This is software emulation, unlike open_agb_firm using native GBA hardware.

Run GBA games and homebrew on the 3DS built-in GBA hardware, with direct SD saves and a ROM browser.

Original and New 3DS/2DS with Luma3DS or fastboot3DS. Extract the package, copy open_agb_firm.firm into /luma/payloads/ and merge its 3ds folder at the SD root; hold START at boot to choose it. Supply legally dumped .gba files; no external GBA BIOS download is required. Uses native hardware: no save states or GBA link cable, games over 32 MiB unsupported, sleep mode incomplete and reboot required between games. Back up old /3ds/open_agb_firm/config.ini before recreating it for this changed config format.

A native 3DS port of GameYob for Game Boy and Game Boy Color games.

Supply your own .gb / .gbc ROM dumps and follow this 3DS port’s README. Optional boot-ROM support requires your own corresponding dump. Use this CIA/3DSX release rather than the separate DS-mode GameYob package. Game compatibility varies.
Mega Drive / Genesis and Sega CD emulation, ported for original 3DS and 2DS hardware.

Preserve the release ZIP’s supplied support files. For Sega CD, put your own region-matched BIOS in /3ds/picodrive_3ds/bios/ as bios_CD_U.bin, bios_CD_J.bin or bios_CD_E.bin. Supply your own ROM/disc dumps. CD games are slower on original hardware; 32X is practical only on New 3DS using the CIA build. Read the project’s game-format notes.
PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16 emulation for the original 3DS family.

Preserve the release files and supply your own HuCard/disc dumps. For CD games, place your own System Card BIOS under /3ds/temperpce_3ds/syscards/, named syscard1.pce, syscard2.pce or syscard3.pce as appropriate; choose it in settings. Match the documented disc-track format. Compatibility varies by title.
An NES / Famicom emulator designed for original 3DS and 2DS systems.

Preserve the ZIP’s support files; install CIA on CFW or launch 3DSX. Supply your own NES/Famicom ROM dumps. FDS games additionally need your own BIOS at /3ds/virtuanes_3ds/bios/disksys.rom. This original release is separate from the Download Play fork.

A complete homebrew arcade game inspired by Super Hexagon: dodge rotating walls and survive.
Extract the 3DS package and use its SuperHaxagon.3dsx in /3ds or install SuperHaxagon.cia. Assets are bundled; no commercial game files or BIOS are needed. Use the included README for 3DS controls.

Doom engine port for 3DS with stereoscopic view controls.

Prerelease v0.7-alpha. Place prboom.wad plus a legally obtained Doom IWAD (for example doom.wad or doom2.wad) in /3ds/prboom3ds/. The engine download does not include commercial Doom game data; optional PWADs still need their matching IWAD.
Native 3DS port of Quake with the shareware episode, configurable touch controls and network multiplayer.

Extract the entire ctrQuake.zip to the SD root to retain its runtime folders and shareware game data, then launch the included 3DSX from Homebrew Launcher or install the separate CIA. The full game requires pak1.pak from your own Quake copy in the ctrQuake/id1 folder. Original-model controls use ABXY to look; the C-Stick camera is New 3DS only. Most multiplayer servers require the full game. No BIOS is required.
A standalone sliding-tile puzzle game with an on-console leaderboard.
Copy the 3DSX into /3ds/ and use Homebrew Launcher. No commercial game data or BIOS is required.
A native 3DS port of the small crafting and survival game Minicraft.
Use the published 3DSX through Homebrew Launcher. This is Minicraft homebrew, separate from commercial Minecraft: New Nintendo 3DS Edition. No Minecraft installation or BIOS is required.
A compact homebrew arcade game: guide the bird through gaps and beat your score.
Install the CIA on CFW or launch the 3DSX from /3ds/. This standalone homebrew release does not require a commercial game installation or BIOS.
A homebrew snake game with local wireless multiplayer.

Install the CIA on CFW or use its 3DSX in Homebrew Launcher. Check the project controls and local-play instructions; multiplayer requires compatible nearby systems and wireless. No commercial game data or BIOS is supplied or required. The publisher labels this release beta.

A menu for DS-mode homebrew and nds-bootstrap. Choose the Flashcard package for a DS / DS Lite flashcart, or the DSi package for a prepared DSi SD card.
DS(i) loading backend used by TWiLight Menu++. Normally update it through your menu; standalone files are here for documented manual setups.
Browse files, inspect data and back up supported cartridges or saves. Cartridge access depends on the model and launch method; DSi Slot-1 dumping requires Unlaunch.
Transfer files over a local wireless network using an FTP client. Launch the NDS build through your compatible DS homebrew setup and connect to the address it displays.
Homebrew Menu · hbmenu original DS menu icon
devkitPro’s file browser and launcher for native DS homebrew.
DS / DS Lite flashcart · DSi via supported homebrew route
Extract the release and use BOOT.NDS with the bootstrap appropriate to your flashcart or existing homebrew route.
Place additional homebrew in /nds/ and keep required app data in the paths its publisher specifies. Read the release README before choosing a flashcart boot file.
This is a launcher for an already supported entry point, not a DSi exploit or a 3DS CIA installer. Bootstrap selection depends on the flashcart.
The original ready bundle also includes bootstrap.cia for a separate 3DS route. On DS/DSi use BOOT.NDS and the relevant flashcart bootstrap; do not install the CIA.

A native diagnostic for buttons, touchscreen, microphone and battery status.
DS / DS Lite flashcart · DSi / XL · 3DS DS mode
Copy cg-input-test.nds to your flashcart microSD or prepared console SD, then launch it as native NDS homebrew.
No separate data folder is required. /roms/nds/homebrew/ is an optional organizational folder.
Battery information depends on hardware and launch mode; original DS hardware only exposes a high/low battery state.

Cereal Box Snow original DS menu icon
A creative particle simulator with snow, fire, rain, birds and fireflies.

Copy CerealBoxSnowNds1.2.0.nds to your homebrew storage, for example /roms/nds/homebrew/, then open it in a compatible homebrew launcher. This folder is a library suggestion, not a fixed app requirement.
Use the touchscreen and on-screen controls. In the NDS build, X or Up switches between attracting and pushing particles.
Select this Nintendo DS executable. The Windows and Linux releases are separate desktop apps and are not included in the console download.

NitrousTracker · music studio original DS menu icon
A stylus-operated XM music tracker and sampler, with pattern editing and microphone recording.
DS / DS Lite flashcart · DSi via compatible homebrew launcher
Extract the ready ZIP. Copy nitroustracker.nds and the supplied songs/ and themes/ folders to your SD card. Launch nitroustracker.nds; debug and MIDI variants remain preserved in the original ZIP.
Use the app’s file browser to load or save .xm songs and .wav samples in folders of your choice. Keep copies of your songs before upgrading the app.
This pins the ready 0.6.5 GitHub release. Later builds, including native 3DS and beta releases, have separate packages; they are not substituted for this DS build.
Samples must be uncompressed 8-bit or 16-bit WAV. Memory available for samples is smaller in DS mode than in DSi mode.

dsidl · DSi QR downloader original DS menu icon
A DSi-camera utility for downloading a file from a URL encoded in a QR code.
DSi / DSi XL · DSi mode only
Copy dsidl.dsi to the DSi SD card and open it with a DSi-mode homebrew launcher. A DS / DS Lite flashcart cannot provide its required camera and DSi Wi-Fi functions.
Configure Wi-Fi through System Settings → Advanced Settings. Scan a QR containing a URL, then choose the SD destination folder and filename in dsidl.

The publisher labels v0.1.1 as a prerelease. Requires a working DSi camera, SD access and a compatible router. Its dsiwifi library has router limitations; the author says WEP/open networks may not work. Hold SELECT at launch for connection logs.

dslibris · EPUB reader official project artwork
A two-screen ebook reader for DS, DSi and DSi XL, with bookmarks and configurable TrueType fonts.
DS / DS Lite flashcart · DSi / DSi XL
Extract dslibris.nds, Font/ and Book/ to the storage root, keeping that exact layout. Do not put them inside a new app subfolder.
Place your EPUB books in /Book/ and optional .ttf fonts in /Font/. Launch dslibris.nds from the homebrew menu.
Some flashcarts need the matching DLDI patch. This is the published v1.5.2-2 release; the separate v1.6.0 prerelease is not substituted. The upstream repository is archived.

DSi camera test original DS menu icon
A small camera utility that previews the DSi’s cameras and saves 640×480 PNG photos.
Copy dsi-camera.nds onto the DSi SD card and open it with a launcher that provides DSi-mode camera and SD access.
Saved photos use /DCIM/100DSI00/IMG_####.PNG. Keep existing photos and available space on the card.

The .nds extension does not make this a DS / DS Lite camera app: it requires the DSi hardware cameras. The publisher supplies a separate CIA asset for another installation route; it is not included here.

An updated ebook reader for EPUB, FB2 and text books, with fonts, encodings and bookmarks.
DS / DS Lite flashcart · DSi / XL direct boot or hiyaCFW
Extract sdcard-root.zip into the SD root, retaining /books/ and /data/ikureader/ with its fonts, encodings and translations.
Use IkuReader.nds for DS flashcarts, or IkuReader.dsi for the publisher’s DSi direct-boot/hiyaCFW route. Keep your books and /data/ikureader/bookmarks/ when updating.
The data ZIP is required alongside the selected executable. Preserve the supplied fonts and encoding tables; this page keeps both original console variants separately.

Open the NDS or DSi build through the launcher specified by the project. GodMode9i’s cartridge functions have additional model-specific access requirements.

This is a Windows PC-host setup for the BO2 Resurge or Microsoft Store client. The source describes a UDP relay for friends joining a custom game behind NAT. It does not establish PS4/PS5 game compatibility. The associated packages are not offered here while their distribution/capture review remains incomplete.
Install Wireshark with Npcap selected, then install WinPcap 4.1.3. The source calls for both capture drivers, in that order. Reboot after both installations.
Confirm that Wireshark lists the active Ethernet or Wi-Fi interface. The source runs RUN_GUI.exe with administrator privileges.
Keep the relay package, supported PC game client and access to the router configuration available.
Record the host and gateway addresses
Run ipconfig in Command Prompt. Under the active adapter, note IPv4 Address for the host PC and Default Gateway for the router. The tutorial recommends a DHCP reservation or static host address.
Open the default gateway address and find Port Forwarding/NAT. Forward external UDP 3074 to internal UDP 3077 at the host PC’s IPv4 address. Enable and save the rule.
Open the custom game before starting the relay
Open the relay tool as administrator. Set Game Port to 3074 and Relay Port to 3077. Do not choose Start yet.
Launch the supported PC client and open a Custom Game lobby/map first.
Return to RUN_GUI and choose Start. Check the traffic/log output, then have a friend test joining through the public address or the client’s normal invite method.
The source offers a VPS with public IPv4 when home forwarding is unavailable, including CGNAT/shared-network setups.
It opens inbound UDP 3074 and 3077 in both provider and operating-system firewalls, with outbound UDP permitted.
Its alternatives are the same relay on the VPS pointed at the home/public or VPN address, or WireGuard forwarding VPS UDP 3074 to the home client’s UDP 3077. Friends join the VPS public address.
The Windows machine running RUN_GUI still needs the packet-capture drivers.
For missing traffic, check both capture drivers, required permissions, the selected active network interface and the custom-game-before-Start order.
For join failures, check UDP forwarding, the host address, double NAT and CGNAT. Use a UDP-specific test rather than a TCP-only port checker.
If the setup stops working after a reboot, confirm that the host PC address has not changed. Preserve the full error text and relay logs when reporting a problem.

MWR-specific setup from the supplied guide
Keep the Tools folder and other supplied files together. In the launcher, choose the Modern Warfare Remastered tool.
Enable GoldHEN and its bin loader, launch Modern Warfare Remastered update 1.15 and open Multiplayer.
On the tool Home page, enter the PS4 IP address and use Send ps4debug (Envoyer ps4debug), port 9090. Wait for the console notification, then choose Connect (Connecter).
On the GSC Injector page, leave the .gscbin field empty to select the built-in MAG menu.

Stay at the Multiplayer main menu, enable Auto inject (Injection auto), and keep the tool open and connected. The guide explains that MWR restarts its Multiplayer process between menus and matches, so automatic injection restores the menu.
Start a private match as host; the menu loads with the map. Remove (Retirer) at the Multiplayer menu or restart the game to unload it.

In the menu, use GameMode → AI Zombies and choose a map. The source recommends a private team match, such as Team Deathmatch. The match restarts followed by two ten-second countdowns; selecting an AI Zombies entry again stops the mode.
AI Zombies map choices in the guide
Backlot, Ambush, Bloc, Vacant, Overgrown, Crash, Bog, Countdown, Crossfire, District, Downpour, Pipeline, Shipment, Showdown, Strike and Wet Work.
The Compilation card accepts a .gsc file or a folder of .gsc files, then compiles a .gscbin.
Define init(); the guide says it is called for matches and the menu lobby. Its menu-lobby map name is mp_vlobby_room, where the script should return immediately.
Supported includes are maps\mp\_utility, maps\mp\gametypes\_hud_util and common_scripts\utility in compiler\include.
The stated limit is 128 KB of bytecode per script. Fully restart MWR if the tool reports that the injection area is full.
The source identifies gsc-tool as the compiler, licensed GPL-3.0; its license file is included in the archive.
The Journal card and MAG_GSC_INJECTOR_MWR.log beside the executable record each step. Developers credited by the MWR guide: UrBaaZz and Zerty.

Cheat labels and conditions from this exact file

TRAINER INFO (read only): BE SURE TO READ ALL the comments where available. As a rule of thumb (for all games), ALWAYS enable only cheats that are needed and disable when they are not. You may need to enable Player-No-Dead cheat to prevent dying from fall damage when using the Moon/Super-Jump cheat. For an even more advanced trainer, check out my MultiTrainer2 ShnExt trainer. This trainer was made and tested on PS4 Firmware 9.00, but should also work on other firmwares. Credits: Some cheats were ported or derived from older game versions cheats made by TLH and/or Rizla and from the PC trainer made by FLiNG. Enjoy! ;-)

---One Hit Kill (requires MC): Using OHK on specific bosses, such as the first Goblin in Hogsmeade will cause progression issues. Also, deactive the cheat when practicing in Hogwarts, especially with dummies (eg. The Chinese chomping cabbage practice) as you may not be able to complete the training. If you get stuck after killing an enemy, disable OHK and reload the last save to complete the fight without it, then you may re-activate the cheat.

Infinite Ancient Magic: Using OHK on specific bosses, such as the first Goblin in Hogsmeade will cause progression issues. Also, deactive the cheat when practicing in Hogwarts, especially with dummies (eg. The Chinese chomping cabbage practice) as you may not be able to complete the training. If you get stuck after killing an enemy, disable OHK and reload the last save to complete the fight without it, then you may re-activate the cheat.
Infinite Items: Works for most items, including potions, resources etc
Infinite Items Usage: Takes effect when you use an item, the item amount won't decrease. Works for most usable items, such as potios.
Instant Brew Potions: Activate before brewing a potion.
Instant Grow Plants: Active before planting seeds.
---Ignore Conjuration Requirements (requires MC): When activated, you can craft items using the conjuring spell even if you don't have enough resources. If you do have resources, they will be used.

Teleport To Map Waypoint: Enable Infinite HP cheat as a precaution. After being teleported, wait a few seconds for rendering to complete. When its done, press X + DPAD DOWN to continue. If you get teleported BELOW THE MAP after the game completes rendering, first press X + DPAD UP to lift you above the map and then press X + DPAD DOWN to continue. If for any reason you end up falling infinitely below the map, exit the game and re-launch it. AVOID teleporting yourself to places that are still locked, which you are not suppose to be able to reach yet, as this may cause game progession issue or other issues. DOESNT WORK IN FLY MODE.

---Unlock All Fast Travel Locations (requires MC): When activated, you can fast travel to any fast travel locations, even if they're still locked. If you fast traveled to a locked location, it will then be unlocked.

Stealth Mode: Enemies will be able to see you only after they get attacked. Note that this cheat has not been thoroughly tested and might cause progression issues, especially in case a fight is required to progress, thus enemies need to detect you first (boss fights likely).In such cases, you may need to disable the cheat and continue or restart from the last checkpoint with the cheat disabled.

Undetectable: Enemies can not detect you and will not attack back when being hit. Note that this cheat has not been thoroughly tested and might cause progression issues, especially in case a fight is required to progress, thus enemies need to detect you first (boss fights likely). In such cases, you may need to disable the cheat and continue or restart from the last checkpoint with the cheat disabled.
0 Quidditch Trial Timer: Scoreboard will display 1 Second

Gain Max Money (READ INFO): When activated, shop items will cost negative money, which mean you will gain money when buying from shops. This is a one time use cheat. Be sure to enable it ONLY right before starting shopping and disable it immediately after completing shopping. Do not enable the cheat after gaining sufficient funds. 10 million coins are usually enough for the entire game.
99 Talent Points: Takes effect when you open the Talents menu or when you spend talent points.

Open your PS3 archive over HTTP

The local archive server runs on the computer holding your backup. It offers PS3 console files and original archives through plain HTTP, including large PKGs that are not mirrored on the website. Windows RTM helpers, source code and other consoles stay outside this list.
Open a terminal in the site checkout and run the command below. Replace the example address with that computer’s private LAN IPv4 address. Keep this terminal running while files transfer.
In the PS3 browser, visit the printed HTTP address on port 8766. The console and computer must be on the same LAN. Choose a PS3 package, game file or original archive from the separate lists.

Use an ordinary file link, browse the HTTP list in ezRemote, or select Save with webMAN when webMAN MOD is already active on the PS3. The webMAN link downloads to /dev_hdd0/packages; it does not install or run the file.

Install an appropriate PS3 PKG through the supported Package Manager workflow. Extract original ZIP/RAR/7z files first. SPRX, EBOOT and script files still need their documented game update, build and destination.
Addresses refer to the device opening them.
for testing on the archive computer. For your console, use the computer’s private LAN address. The PS3 cannot browse a Windows F: path directly.

The server only reads allowlisted PS3 files. It supports byte-range downloads for compatible clients. It does not extract, install, run or upload files, and it does not change your firewall settings. Keep storage available for both the original download and any extracted or installed copy.

The default address opens the archive on this computer. Enter its LAN IP when opening this page on the PS3.

as the HTTP server type, and use

Prepare the console and USB drive
Check Settings > System Settings > System Information. Back up saves. Prepare a FAT32 USB drive; formatting a drive erases its existing files.
Extract the supplied archive. Place its validated update PUP at
on the USB drive. Do not copy the RAR archive itself to that path.

Insert the USB drive and choose Settings > System Update > Update via Storage Media. Confirm the displayed update is the intended HFW release. If it is not detected or a same-version install is refused, follow the release’s recovery-mode instructions.

After the firmware installation finishes, open the PS3 Internet Browser and visit the HEN installer linked above. Turn off Confirm Browser Close in the browser Tools settings as directed by the installer.

Choose Initialize HEN installer, then Install HEN when initialization succeeds. Let the installer complete and follow its reboot prompt. Use the official alternate installer instructions if this route fails.
Enable HEN after starting the console
Use Enable HEN under Game on the XMB. Wait for its success notification before launching homebrew. Install compatible PKG apps through the available Package Manager.

Browse console files, manage archives and packages, and use the project’s network tools.
PS5 native folder module, PPSA99109. Publisher installation uses dump_installer and a home-screen launch; its pinned README/release does not supply a firmware test matrix.

This ZIP has eboot.bin, sce_module and sce_sys at its root. Extract all four files into a folder such as PPSA99109, place that folder under /homebrew on the selected USB drive or /data/homebrew on the console, install with dump_installer, then launch its home-screen tile.
Manage supported homebrew and backup layouts. The project requires its unjail payload.

PS5 native module PPSA99110; requires SvenGDK's unjail daemon on a firmware it supports. The daemon must be running before the app starts and must be sent again after a reboot. PS1/PS2/PSP launch functions additionally require the separate emulator resources.

Extract the included PPSA99110 folder and copy it intact to USB /homebrew/PPSA99110 or internal /data/homebrew/PPSA99110. Register with dump_installer, send the author's unjail payload before opening, and use Diagnostics to check actual reachable storage. EmulatorPack.zip is a separate dependency for emulator launch features.
Inspect DualSense sticks, drift, buttons, triggers, touchpad and motion input.
PS5 native title PPSA98766. Publisher requires a jailbroken PS5, kstuff, ShadowMountPlus and an ELF loader on port 9021. No firmware number is specified in the pinned README.

Extract and copy the complete PPSA98766 folder to /data/homebrew/PPSA98766; preserve 0777 permissions on its files. Keep sce_module/libc.prx and sce_sys. The author's separate DriftCheck.elf installer is an alternative upstream download, rather than this ZIP being a payload.
Display test patterns to inspect screen geometry, colour uniformity and pixels.

PS5 native title PPSA69420; the author requires a jailbroken PS5 with ShadowMountPlus. This release is a native app-folder build, rather than the removed websrv/elfldr payload build. The pinned README gives no firmware matrix.
Extract the PPSA69420 folder intact to /data/homebrew/PPSA69420. ShadowMountPlus adds its home-screen tile. Keep eboot.bin, sce_module/libc.prx and sce_sys; close the app using the PS button.
Manage console files and connect through the project’s FTP, SFTP and web tools.

PS5 native title PPSA96024. Requires ShadowMountPlus and elfldr listening on port 9021 at app startup for full storage access. The author reports testing on firmware 13.60; other firmware is untested in the pinned README.

Copy the complete PPSA96024 folder to /data/homebrew/PPSA96024 and preserve 0777 on the folder and every file. Launch from the dashboard with elfldr active. Its start screen reports whether full storage access succeeded; closing the app stops its servers.
Browse internet radio stations, save favourites and control playback with DualSense.

PS5 native media app PPSA99001, content version 01.000.010. Publisher says it is tested on PS5 but supplies no firmware-specific matrix for this release. Internet access is required to browse and stream stations.

Extract and copy the entire PPSA99001 folder to /data/homebrew/PPSA99001 using your compatible PS5 homebrew app loader. Keep its runtime libraries, assets and helpers. The setup guide says not to leave a same-title FFPFSC image from an earlier release beside this folder; automatic updater compatibility is unverified.
Play audio discs using supported USB CD hardware and the project’s music interface.

PS5 native media app PPSA98427. Requires a compatible active homebrew environment and an external USB optical drive that reads audio CDs; it does not use the PS5's internal drive. The author tested Apple USB SuperDrive on firmware 13.60. A local ELF loader on port 9021 may be needed for its access helper.

Copy the full PPSA98427 folder under /data/homebrew so eboot.bin is directly at /data/homebrew/PPSA98427/eboot.bin, then launch CD Player from Media. Preserve 0777 permissions and its title-specific lapy.elf helper. Boot with the external drive empty, then insert the audio CD after boot.
Test HDMI audio formats and speaker channels using the project’s passthrough tools.

PS5 native app PPSA99051. Publisher tested the passthrough sample on a jailbroken PS5 Pro, firmware 12.70, launched through ShadowMountPlus. HDMI bitstream tests require an audio chain that supports the selected codec. The project says its app runs inside its ordinary sandbox.

The selected release ZIP contains the complete PPSA99051 native app folder. Copy that folder under /data/homebrew/PPSA99051 for ShadowMountPlus. Preserve its runtime and indexed audio clips. The sample README also describes a separate FFPFSC build; that is not the format of this selected ZIP.
Control your configured Home Assistant rooms and devices from the console.
PS5 native media app PPSA11019 for a console that runs homebrew. Requires a reachable Home Assistant server and authorized account or access token. The pinned README supplies no firmware test matrix.

Copy the complete PPSA11019 folder to /data/homebrew/PPSA11019 for your compatible loader, then open Home5 from Media. Enter the Home Assistant server's actual IP address and port; the author says homeassistant.local does not resolve on PS5. Sign in within the app and create your rooms manually.
Browse websites with controller navigation, tabs and bookmarks in a native PS5 app.

Experimental PS5 native browser PRWB00001. Requires a jailbroken PS5 with etaHEN or kstuff, ShadowMountPlus, and privileged elfldr at 127.0.0.1:9021; websrv on 8080 is a fallback. The author reports testing only firmware 13.42. The 160.6 MiB ZIP requires manual transfer/extraction outside the site's 32 MiB browser verification limit.

Manually extract the complete PRWB00001 folder so its eboot.bin is at /data/homebrew/PRWB00001/eboot.bin. Keep prosperoweb.elf, prosperoweb-broker.elf, runtime modules, assets and licenses. Launch the native home-screen tile after ShadowMountPlus scans it; sending the browser ELF directly to Payload Manager/elfldr can create an invisible background browser instead.
Native PS5 Moonlight-style client for streaming games or a desktop from a Sunshine-compatible PC. Pair your own host; PC games are streamed, not installed on the PS5.
Native PS5 app, PPSA99002. Requires an already compatible homebrew environment and title loader plus a reachable Sunshine-compatible host. The pinned README gives no universal firmware matrix.

Close the app before updating. Extract the complete PPSA99002/ folder into /data/homebrew/, keep one installation of this title and refresh title registration in your compatible loader. Start Sunshine on your PC, select or add its address in ProsperoLight and enter the pairing PIN on the host. A wired LAN is recommended. Touchpad + L1 ends a stream. Pairings/settings normally stay in /data/prosperolight.
PS5 homebrew store for native recompiled ports, emulators and apps. Game setup uses your own disc images or other required source files; no commercial game data is in this download.
Native PS5 app, PPSA92000. Publisher requires kstuff, an ELF loader on TCP 9021 and ShadowMountPlus 1.7 Beta 5 or newer. No firmware range is inferred from these prerequisites.

Manual install: extract the complete PPSA92000/ directory into /data/homebrew/ and let ShadowMountPlus register the title. Alternatively use the separately archived matching RecompStore-Installer.elf. The installer fetches the newest upstream build when online, or uses its embedded copy offline; use this pinned ZIP for an exact v2.7.4 install. Keep required data, modules and included payloads together. Follow each port’s own game-input requirements.
Standalone publisher installer for the matching PS5 store, separate from the manual app ZIP.

Requires kstuff, an active PS5 ELF loader on TCP 9021 and ShadowMountPlus 1.7 Beta 5 or newer. Explicitly send this ELF with your supported payload sender. Start with a working ELF boot method

A downloaded ELF does not make an unmodified PS2 boot homebrew. Use the model-specific FMCB/OpenTuna guidance above, then launch apps through wLaunchELF or a configured menu. No region bypass is required by these homebrew downloads; the boot method still depends on your model and ROM.
Use a conservative USB starting point

FAT32 USB is the starting layout for these instructions. PS2ME explicitly requires it. Memory Card Annihilator’s mca_new supports exFAT. Do not assume that an older app gains exFAT, SMB or MX4SIO support because OPL can use a device.

Extract ZIP or TAR.GZ files on your computer before copying them. SuperTux needs its APPS tree at the USB root. PicoDrive needs its skin/config files. A direct ELF is only convenient where its optional or external dependencies are explained on its card.
Separate USB, SMB and internal HDD support

OPL 1.1.0 offers USB, SMB and internal HDD routes; these are OPL features, not universal app services. Internal-HDD tools need a real internal drive interface. The Quake ports document their own USB/APA-PFS loading paths. SMB requires working Ethernet and share settings.
Bring the right data and saves

NES cartridge ROMs, Mega CD BIOS files, Java JARs and Quake PAKs are different requirements. They are not included in these runtime downloads. SuperTux includes its free game data. Keep an original save backup and a memory card available for apps that save there.

Use a PS2 pad for the documented controls. Follow each app’s PAL/NTSC options; do not force an unsupported display mode. PadOS normal is 4:3 with Widescreen OFF. A theme changes OPL’s interface and does not patch game rendering.

Packages were checked for their paths, CRCs where applicable and ELF32 little-endian MIPS executable headers. SHA-256 values identify the exact downloaded bytes. No downloaded executable was run and no physical-console installation or performance test was performed.

Back up original physical-card saves before importing or applying patches. Apollo supports physical memory cards and supported VMC images; follow its documented save-format rules.
Tool, emulator and game illustrations are original SVG artwork made for this catalogue; they are not gameplay captures. Theme previews are the maintainers’ screenshots.

Install Decky Loader and your first plugin
Decky adds a plugin menu to Game Mode. Start with its stable release and install plugins through the built-in store.
In Desktop Mode, open Decky's official site, download the installer, and follow its stable-release installation instructions.
Return to Game Mode, press the three-dot Quick Access button, and select the Decky plug tab.
Open the store icon, search for the plugin's exact name, and select Install.
Open the installed plugin from the Decky tab. Check Decky and plugin updates after Steam client changes.
PowerTools is advanced manual tuning, with no guaranteed FPS gain. ProtonDB Badges shows community reports, separate from Valve's Deck Verified rating.
Customize Steam menus and game artwork
Use CSS Loader for interface themes and SteamGridDB for game artwork. Both install through Decky's store in Game Mode.
Open Quick Access, select the Decky plug tab, and open its store. Install CSS Loader and SteamGridDB.
Open CSS Loader from the Decky tab, browse its theme collection, and enable the theme you want to try.
For artwork, open a game's context menu from your library or its settings cog, then choose Change Artwork.
Browse SteamGridDB's images or select a local image. Check the result in your library before changing other games.
Try one interface theme at a time so you can identify and disable it if a Steam update changes the layout.
Install GE-Proton and select it for one game
ProtonUp-Qt manages additional compatibility tools. Install a version first, then choose it separately for the game that needs it.
In Desktop Mode, install ProtonUp-Qt from Discover or use the Linux download on its official site.
Open ProtonUp-Qt, select your Steam installation, choose Add version, and select the GE-Proton version you need.
Wait for installation to finish, then fully restart Steam so it can find the new compatibility tool.
Open the game's Properties, select Compatibility, enable the specific compatibility-tool option, and select the installed GE-Proton version.
Compatibility varies by game. Keep a working configuration available and test changes one game at a time.
Choose a launcher for non-Steam Windows games
Choose the workflow that matches your game's source. Heroic, Lutris, and Bottles each manage their own installations and settings.
Use Heroic for your Epic, GOG, or Amazon library. Sign into the relevant service and install a game you own.
Use Lutris for a supported game installer or another collection. Follow that game's installation instructions and test its launcher entry.
Use Bottles for a separate Windows software environment. Create a Gaming bottle and follow the app's installer instructions inside it.
Once the game works in Desktop Mode, use the launcher's Steam shortcut option where available, then test the shortcut in Game Mode.
Pick one suitable workflow for each installation; adding more launchers does not fix an incompatible game.
Set up emulation and organize your library
Choose EmuDeck or RetroDECK as your starting setup. Steam ROM Manager handles library shortcuts and artwork for an existing collection.
In Desktop Mode, follow EmuDeck's installer guide or install RetroDECK from Discover and complete its first-run setup.
Choose your storage location, then copy your own game dumps and required BIOS files into the setup's documented folders.
Launch one game through the chosen frontend and check its controls before importing a larger library.
If you want individual Steam entries, configure Steam ROM Manager for your emulator paths, preview the results, and save only the shortcuts you want.
EmuDeck and RetroDECK are alternative setups. Their documentation explains supported formats, folder locations, and emulator-specific requirements.
Pair Moonlight with a gaming PC
Moonlight receives the stream on your Deck. Sunshine runs on the gaming PC that renders and launches the games.
Install Sunshine on the host PC using its official instructions, start it, and complete the initial configuration.
Install Moonlight on the Deck and connect both devices to the same local network for the first pairing.
Open Moonlight and select the PC. If it is not discovered, add the PC's local IP address manually.
Enter the PIN shown by Moonlight in Sunshine's PIN page on the host, then select a game or application to test.
Keep the host PC running while streaming. Confirm local play works before following the projects' separate remote-network instructions.
Register a PS4 or PS5 with chiaki-ng
Set up your own PlayStation console first, then register chiaki-ng. Start with the Deck and console on the same home network.
Enable Remote Play in your console's settings. Use the official configuration guide for the different PS4 and PS5 menu paths.
Install and open chiaki-ng in Desktop Mode. Keep the console powered on and select it when it is discovered.
Follow chiaki-ng's PSN account and registration guide. Use its automatic registration flow or the documented console-link PIN method.
Confirm the console is marked registered, then open it and test a game locally before configuring optional rest-mode wake or remote access.
Use the guide matching your console and chosen registration method; account registration and console pairing are separate setup steps.
Move files between your Deck and another device
LocalSend transfers files over your local network. Install it on both devices and keep its receive window available on the destination.
Install LocalSend on the Deck in Desktop Mode and on the phone or computer holding your files.
Connect both devices to the same local network and open LocalSend on each device so they can discover one another.
On the sending device, choose the files, select Send, and pick the receiving device's displayed name.
Confirm the incoming transfer on the receiving device. Wait for completion, then open its receive folder and check the files.
If discovery fails, check the project's network troubleshooting instructions. A guest Wi-Fi network may separate connected devices.
Fix a Flatpak folder permission or game dependency
Use Flatseal for a specific app's folder access. Use Protontricks only when a game's instructions require a Windows component or prefix change.
Close the affected application, open Flatseal, and select that application's entry rather than changing permissions for every app.
For an inaccessible library folder, add only its required path under Filesystem, Other files. Use read-only access when sufficient.
Restart the affected app and test access. Use Flatseal's Reset button if your permission changes cause problems.
For a documented Protontricks fix, launch the game once through Steam with its selected Proton tool, close it, then select it in Protontricks.
Apply only the components or actions named by the game's instructions, then test the game again.
Sync a selected folder with Syncthing
Set up a shared folder between your own devices. Start with a small test folder before choosing a game-save or document folder.
In Desktop Mode, unpack the official Linux AMD64 build and start its syncthing executable following the project guide. Start Syncthing on your other device too.
Open the local browser interface shown by Syncthing. Add the other device using its device ID, and accept the matching device on that device.
Add a folder with the path you want to share. Select the paired device, then accept the shared folder and choose its destination on the receiving device.
Copy a test file into the shared folder and wait for both devices to report that they are up to date. Keep Syncthing running while you need synchronization.
Sync propagates edits and deletions. Keep independent save backups; optional versioning archives incoming changes and is configured separately on each device.
Inspect and extract an archive with PeaZip
Use Desktop Mode to browse a download before extracting it into a chosen folder.
Unpack the official portable Linux Qt6 build and open PeaZip from the extracted application folder, following its Linux setup notes.
Open the archive in PeaZip and review the file list. For a multipart archive, keep all supplied parts together.
Choose Extract, select a new destination folder, and review the overwrite and output options. Keep deletion of the original archive disabled.
Complete extraction and check the output folder in Dolphin. Keep the original archive and use the extracted files only as directed by their project.
Inspect disk usage and game caches
Filelight maps folders in Desktop Mode. Storage Cleaner shows per-game cache and compatibility-data usage through Decky.
Install Filelight from Discover in Desktop Mode. Scan your home folder or the drive you want to inspect.
Explore larger segments of the ring map to identify the folders using space. Review their paths and contents before making changes.
For Game Mode inspection, install Storage Cleaner through Decky's stable store, then open it from the Decky tab.
Read the per-game shader-cache and compatibility-data sizes. Leave cleanup actions untouched while you identify the data and check your backups.
Compatibility folders can contain saves and settings. Shader caches may regenerate after removal, so clearing them is not a permanent storage saving.
Organize library tabs and compare game lengths
TabMaster customizes your library tabs. HLTB for Deck adds completion-time estimates to game pages.
Install TabMaster and HLTB for Deck from Decky's stable plugin store in Game Mode.
Open TabMaster in Quick Access. Add or edit a tab, then choose a collection, installed-game, or platform filter for the titles you want to see.
Reorder or hide tabs as needed, then return to the library and check the result.
Open a game page to see its HowLongToBeat estimates. Use View Details to inspect the source listing, and adjust the bar's appearance in the HLTB plugin menu.
Completion times are community estimates. HLTB data can become temporarily unavailable when its upstream service changes.
Reconnect Bluetooth devices from your game
Pair a device once in Steam Settings, then use the Bluetooth plugin as a Quick Access shortcut.
Open Steam Settings, select Bluetooth, enable it, and pair your headphones or controller using the normal Steam interface.
Open Quick Access with the three-dot button, select Decky, and install Bluetooth from its stable plugin store.
Open Bluetooth in the Decky tab and select your already paired device to reconnect it.
Check that the controller or headphones work in your game. If the device is missing, return to Steam Settings and confirm its pairing.
The plugin connects existing pairings; it does not replace initial device pairing in Steam Settings.
Pause and resume an offline game
Use manual pause first so you can check how a game behaves before enabling focus-based automation.
Install Pause Games from the stable Decky store, launch an offline game, and save your progress.
Open Quick Access, select Decky, then open Pause Games to see its running-game list.
Select the game icon with the pause symbol to stop it. Select its play symbol to resume, then check controls and audio.
If manual pausing works, optionally enable Pause on focus loss. Test switching apps and turn the option off if the game freezes or loses input.
This stops running processes; it does not save their state to disk or release their RAM/VRAM. Network sessions may time out while paused. Save frequently.
Install a Steam menu sound pack
Audio Loader uses a curated Pack Manager to install sound packs for the Steam interface.
Install Audio Loader from the stable Decky store, then open it from the Decky tab in Quick Access.
While connected to the internet, open the plugin's Pack Manager and browse the available sound packs.
Install a pack and select it in Audio Loader. Navigate the Steam menus to check its sound effects.
Try one pack at a time. Return to Audio Loader to disable or change the selected pack if you want different menu sounds.
Menu sound packs are separate from game audio. Use the plugin manager rather than manually copying theme folders.
Animation Changer manages installed startup animations and can choose a different one each boot.
Install Animation Changer from Decky's stable plugin store and open it from Quick Access.
Open its animation browser, choose a startup animation from SteamDeckRepo, and install it.
Select the installed animation in the plugin. Check Steam Settings > Customization if a different Startup Movie overrides it; follow the project's current setting instructions.
Restart the Deck when convenient to check the result. Enable randomization only if you want to rotate through your installed animations.
The built-in browser supplies startup animations. Suspend-animation configuration is a separate advanced feature described by the project.
Check Flatpak app updates in Game Mode
Start with manual update checks before deciding whether you want background automation.
Install AutoFlatpaks from Decky's stable plugin store and open it from Quick Access.
Keep automatic upgrading disabled initially. Run a manual check for available Flatpak updates.
Open the package manager to review the apps and runtimes. Select the updates you want, start the queue, and keep the Deck awake until it finishes.
Choose a check interval and notification style if useful. Enable upgrading without user interaction only if you want automatic updates.
The plugin requires root permissions and currently supports system-installed Flatpaks only. It updates Flatpak apps and runtimes, not SteamOS or Steam games.
Open an installed desktop app from Quick Access
Quick Launch opens installed apps in Game Mode and can create Steam library shortcuts.
Install the desktop application you need in Desktop Mode and check its normal setup first.
Return to Game Mode and install Quick Launch from the stable Decky plugin store.
Open Quick Launch from Decky's Quick Access tab, choose an installed app, and launch it.
Close that application before opening another through the plugin. Use the plugin's shortcut action if you also want the app listed in your Steam library.
The author reports limited maintenance and support for one application at a time. If it stops working after a Steam update, add the application to Steam from Desktop Mode instead.

Required software and dependencies for game cheats

Most cheats and tools are built with C# and require the .NET runtime to function. Without it you will see errors like ".NET Framework is not installed." Install the version your tool needs -- .NET 4.8 covers legacy apps while .NET 6 and .NET 8 cover modern ones.

C++ based tools and game mods need Visual C++ runtime libraries. Missing them causes "VCRUNTIME140.dll was not found" and similar DLL errors. The all-in-one package installs every version from 2005 to 2022 in one step.

Some older games and overlays rely on legacy DirectX components not included with Windows. If you see errors mentioning d3dx9_43.dll or xinput1_3.dll, installing the DirectX End-User Runtime from Microsoft will fix them.

Original whatwhatboy preview: Game Mod Safety & Download Security
Important safety information for using gaming tools
Follow these guidelines to stay safe while modding
Keep your antivirus software updated at all times. Scan every file before running it on your system. Use tools like VirusTotal to verify downloads from multiple engines.
Always use alternative accounts for modding and cheating. Never risk your main account. Create dedicated alt accounts specifically for testing modifications.
Only download from trusted and verified sources. Avoid random links, suspicious websites, and unverified third-party downloads. Stick to known communities.
Always use the latest versions of cheats and mods. Outdated tools are more likely to be detected and may contain unpatched security vulnerabilities.
Follow installation guides carefully and completely. Skipping steps can lead to crashes, bans, or security issues. Read all documentation before proceeding.
Always create backups before installing any mods or cheats. Back up game files, save data, and create system restore points so you can recover if something goes wrong.
Understanding why gaming tools trigger security warnings

Cheat software uses injection techniques similar to malware, such as DLL injection and memory modification. This causes antivirus programs to flag them as threats, even when they are legitimate tools from trusted sources.

Add the cheat folder to your antivirus exclusion list before extracting files. In Windows Defender, go to Settings > Virus & Threat Protection > Exclusions and add the folder path. This prevents automatic deletion of legitimate tools.

Upload suspicious files to VirusTotal.com to scan with multiple engines. A few detections among many clean results typically indicates a false positive. If the majority flag it, avoid the file entirely.

Original whatwhatboy preview: Nintendo 3DS Apps & Utilities
Find an app, game or emulator
No resources match. Clear the filters to browse everything.
The six established resources and their pinned releases are preserved.
Custom firmware for the 2DS / 3DS family, including New models. It runs through a persistent exploit such as boot9strap; an archive alone does not install CFW on a stock console.
A full-access file browser for NAND backups, cartridge dumping and system maintenance. Follow its usage guide before making writes to system storage.
Find, install and update homebrew from Universal-DB and other Unistores directly on the console. Includes app search, screenshots and a download queue.
Back up and restore supported game saves and extdata. Use the 3DS CIA on a prepared 2DS / 3DS, and keep an original backup before restoring or editing saves.
Access SD-card files from an FTP client on your local network. This CIA is the 2DS / 3DS build, separate from the Nintendo DS binary.
Launch DS-mode homebrew on a CFW-enabled 2DS / 3DS. Follow the 3DS-specific installation steps; its package differs from the DS flashcard and DSi builds.
Manage HOME Menu themes, boot splashes and badges.

Luma3DS custom firmware; CIA installs to HOME Menu, 3DSX runs through Homebrew Launcher. Theme folders or ZIPs belong in /Themes; splash folders in /Splashes. Open HOME Menu theme settings once first. Region-changed systems must use a functioning HOME Menu/theme extdata for their installed region.
On-console Pokémon save manager and editor with storage banks.

Supported Pokémon save files; back up each save in Checkpoint before editing. It manages saves, it does not supply the games. Internet is used to obtain verified additional assets. See project wiki for exact generation/title/save support.
File manager for browsing and organizing files on the console SD card.

Use stable v5.1.0 rather than the separately published next-v1.00 prerelease. CIA needs custom firmware; 3DSX needs Homebrew Launcher. Keep a PC backup before moving/deleting files, especially Nintendo 3DS and save data.
Read hardware, firmware, battery and system information directly on the handheld.
Runs as CIA on a custom-firmware system or 3DSX in Homebrew Launcher. Useful for identifying the actual Old/New model before choosing model-limited software. No BIOS or game data needed.
Nintendo Homebrew archive of the original FBI title manager release.

Archived FBI 2.6.1 release, not a new fork version. Use on a system already running custom firmware. CIA files are installers; install only software you trust and keep homebrew 3DSX separate from installed titles. Follow 3ds.hacks.guide finalizing setup for initial FBI installation.
Dump the handheld DSP firmware needed by homebrew audio applications.

Creates /3ds/dspfirm.cdc from your own console. Use the DSP1 CIA or 3DSX; DSP2 is an alternative CIA with automatic self-removal and is intentionally not selected here. No downloaded DSP firmware is supplied.
Browse and install actual 3DS/2DS themes, boot splashes and badges from Themezer on the handheld.

Luma3DS custom firmware and a working HOME Menu with Change Theme support. Install the CIA using FBI, or copy the 3DSX to /3ds/ for Homebrew Launcher. Themes use /Themes, splash packages /Splashes and badges /Badges; cache/settings use /3ds/themezer-3ds/. This is the 3DS app, not the Switch NXThemes installer. Region support depends on the installed HOME Menu; do not region-change a console solely to install themes.

Use a genuine SD / microSD with FAT32 and an MBR partition table. The maintained guide recommends 2–128 GB; larger cards can introduce GBA graphics and custom-theme issues. Keep the entire existing Nintendo 3DS folder and your saves backed up.
CIA apps: install to HOME Menu
Copy a CIA to a convenient SD folder such as /cias/, then use FBI on your prepared CFW system to install it. Read the app requirements first. Universal-Updater is another route for supported apps.
Put the executable in /3ds/ or its documented app subfolder. Copy bundled data directories separately to their specified SD paths. A lone 3DSX is not a replacement for required game data.

This is a Windows PC-host setup for the BO2 Resurge or Microsoft Store client. The source describes a UDP relay for friends joining a custom game behind NAT. It does not establish PS4/PS5 game compatibility. The associated packages are not offered here while their distribution/capture review remains incomplete.
Install Wireshark with Npcap selected, then install WinPcap 4.1.3. The source calls for both capture drivers, in that order. Reboot after both installations.
Confirm that Wireshark lists the active Ethernet or Wi-Fi interface. The source runs RUN_GUI.exe with administrator privileges.
Keep the relay package, supported PC game client and access to the router configuration available.
Record the host and gateway addresses
Run ipconfig in Command Prompt. Under the active adapter, note IPv4 Address for the host PC and Default Gateway for the router. The tutorial recommends a DHCP reservation or static host address.
Open the default gateway address and find Port Forwarding/NAT. Forward external UDP 3074 to internal UDP 3077 at the host PC’s IPv4 address. Enable and save the rule.
Open the custom game before starting the relay
Open the relay tool as administrator. Set Game Port to 3074 and Relay Port to 3077. Do not choose Start yet.
Launch the supported PC client and open a Custom Game lobby/map first.
Return to RUN_GUI and choose Start. Check the traffic/log output, then have a friend test joining through the public address or the client’s normal invite method.
The source offers a VPS with public IPv4 when home forwarding is unavailable, including CGNAT/shared-network setups.
It opens inbound UDP 3074 and 3077 in both provider and operating-system firewalls, with outbound UDP permitted.
Its alternatives are the same relay on the VPS pointed at the home/public or VPN address, or WireGuard forwarding VPS UDP 3074 to the home client’s UDP 3077. Friends join the VPS public address.
The Windows machine running RUN_GUI still needs the packet-capture drivers.
For missing traffic, check both capture drivers, required permissions, the selected active network interface and the custom-game-before-Start order.
For join failures, check UDP forwarding, the host address, double NAT and CGNAT. Use a UDP-specific test rather than a TCP-only port checker.
If the setup stops working after a reboot, confirm that the host PC address has not changed. Preserve the full error text and relay logs when reporting a problem.

Windows 10/11 GSC injector with the MAG menu and ps4debug built in.
PS4 Modern Warfare Remastered game update 1.15; GoldHEN with bin loader.
MWR-specific setup from the supplied guide
Keep the Tools folder and other supplied files together. In the launcher, choose the Modern Warfare Remastered tool.
Enable GoldHEN and its bin loader, launch Modern Warfare Remastered update 1.15 and open Multiplayer.
On the tool Home page, enter the PS4 IP address and use Send ps4debug (Envoyer ps4debug), port 9090. Wait for the console notification, then choose Connect (Connecter).
On the GSC Injector page, leave the .gscbin field empty to select the built-in MAG menu.

Stay at the Multiplayer main menu, enable Auto inject (Injection auto), and keep the tool open and connected. The guide explains that MWR restarts its Multiplayer process between menus and matches, so automatic injection restores the menu.
Start a private match as host; the menu loads with the map. Remove (Retirer) at the Multiplayer menu or restart the game to unload it.

In the menu, use GameMode → AI Zombies and choose a map. The source recommends a private team match, such as Team Deathmatch. The match restarts followed by two ten-second countdowns; selecting an AI Zombies entry again stops the mode.
AI Zombies map choices in the guide
Backlot, Ambush, Bloc, Vacant, Overgrown, Crash, Bog, Countdown, Crossfire, District, Downpour, Pipeline, Shipment, Showdown, Strike and Wet Work.
The Compilation card accepts a .gsc file or a folder of .gsc files, then compiles a .gscbin.
Define init(); the guide says it is called for matches and the menu lobby. Its menu-lobby map name is mp_vlobby_room, where the script should return immediately.
Supported includes are maps\mp\_utility, maps\mp\gametypes\_hud_util and common_scripts\utility in compiler\include.
The stated limit is 128 KB of bytecode per script. Fully restart MWR if the tool reports that the injection area is full.
The source identifies gsc-tool as the compiler, licensed GPL-3.0; its license file is included in the archive.
The Journal card and MAG_GSC_INJECTOR_MWR.log beside the executable record each step. Developers credited by the MWR guide: UrBaaZz and Zerty.

TRAINER INFO (read only): BE SURE TO READ ALL the comments where available. As a rule of thumb (for all games), ALWAYS enable only cheats that are needed and disable when they are not. You may need to enable Player-No-Dead cheat to prevent dying from fall damage when using the Moon/Super-Jump cheat. For an even more advanced trainer, check out my MultiTrainer2 ShnExt trainer. This trainer was made and tested on PS4 Firmware 9.00, but should also work on other firmwares. Credits: Some cheats were ported or derived from older game versions cheats made by TLH and/or Rizla and from the PC trainer made by FLiNG. Enjoy! ;-)

---One Hit Kill (requires MC): Using OHK on specific bosses, such as the first Goblin in Hogsmeade will cause progression issues. Also, deactive the cheat when practicing in Hogwarts, especially with dummies (eg. The Chinese chomping cabbage practice) as you may not be able to complete the training. If you get stuck after killing an enemy, disable OHK and reload the last save to complete the fight without it, then you may re-activate the cheat.

Infinite Ancient Magic: Using OHK on specific bosses, such as the first Goblin in Hogsmeade will cause progression issues. Also, deactive the cheat when practicing in Hogwarts, especially with dummies (eg. The Chinese chomping cabbage practice) as you may not be able to complete the training. If you get stuck after killing an enemy, disable OHK and reload the last save to complete the fight without it, then you may re-activate the cheat.
Infinite Items: Works for most items, including potions, resources etc
Infinite Items Usage: Takes effect when you use an item, the item amount won't decrease. Works for most usable items, such as potios.
Instant Brew Potions: Activate before brewing a potion.
Instant Grow Plants: Active before planting seeds.
---Ignore Conjuration Requirements (requires MC): When activated, you can craft items using the conjuring spell even if you don't have enough resources. If you do have resources, they will be used.

Teleport To Map Waypoint: Enable Infinite HP cheat as a precaution. After being teleported, wait a few seconds for rendering to complete. When its done, press X + DPAD DOWN to continue. If you get teleported BELOW THE MAP after the game completes rendering, first press X + DPAD UP to lift you above the map and then press X + DPAD DOWN to continue. If for any reason you end up falling infinitely below the map, exit the game and re-launch it. AVOID teleporting yourself to places that are still locked, which you are not suppose to be able to reach yet, as this may cause game progession issue or other issues. DOESNT WORK IN FLY MODE.

---Unlock All Fast Travel Locations (requires MC): When activated, you can fast travel to any fast travel locations, even if they're still locked. If you fast traveled to a locked location, it will then be unlocked.

Stealth Mode: Enemies will be able to see you only after they get attacked. Note that this cheat has not been thoroughly tested and might cause progression issues, especially in case a fight is required to progress, thus enemies need to detect you first (boss fights likely).In such cases, you may need to disable the cheat and continue or restart from the last checkpoint with the cheat disabled.

Undetectable: Enemies can not detect you and will not attack back when being hit. Note that this cheat has not been thoroughly tested and might cause progression issues, especially in case a fight is required to progress, thus enemies need to detect you first (boss fights likely). In such cases, you may need to disable the cheat and continue or restart from the last checkpoint with the cheat disabled.
0 Quidditch Trial Timer: Scoreboard will display 1 Second

Gain Max Money (READ INFO): When activated, shop items will cost negative money, which mean you will gain money when buying from shops. This is a one time use cheat. Be sure to enable it ONLY right before starting shopping and disable it immediately after completing shopping. Do not enable the cheat after gaining sufficient funds. 10 million coins are usually enough for the entire game.
99 Talent Points: Takes effect when you open the Talents menu or when you spend talent points.

Open your PS3 archive over HTTP

The local archive server runs on the computer holding your backup. It offers PS3 console files and original archives through plain HTTP, including large PKGs that are not mirrored on the website. Windows RTM helpers, source code and other consoles stay outside this list.
Open a terminal in the site checkout and run the command below. Replace the example address with that computer’s private LAN IPv4 address. Keep this terminal running while files transfer.
In the PS3 browser, visit the printed HTTP address on port 8766. The console and computer must be on the same LAN. Choose a PS3 package, game file or original archive from the separate lists.

Use an ordinary file link, browse the HTTP list in ezRemote, or select Save with webMAN when webMAN MOD is already active on the PS3. The webMAN link downloads to /dev_hdd0/packages; it does not install or run the file.

Install an appropriate PS3 PKG through the supported Package Manager workflow. Extract original ZIP/RAR/7z files first. SPRX, EBOOT and script files still need their documented game update, build and destination.
Addresses refer to the device opening them.
for testing on the archive computer. For your console, use the computer’s private LAN address. The PS3 cannot browse a Windows F: path directly.

The server only reads allowlisted PS3 files. It supports byte-range downloads for compatible clients. It does not extract, install, run or upload files, and it does not change your firewall settings. Keep storage available for both the original download and any extracted or installed copy.
Archive computer’s private LAN IPv4 address
The default address opens the archive on this computer. Enter its LAN IP when opening this page on the PS3.
In PS3 ezRemote, set the server URL to the address below, choose
as the HTTP server type, and use
as the remote directory. Browse the resource and build folders to reach the original filenames.

Replace the example computer address with your own. The server provides a separate Apache-format directory because the browser’s styled download page is not an ezRemote directory format. Downloading a remote PKG or creating its install bubble still requires completing the console’s documented package-installation workflow.

Prepare the console and USB drive
Check Settings > System Settings > System Information. Back up saves. Prepare a FAT32 USB drive; formatting a drive erases its existing files.
Extract the supplied archive. Place its validated update PUP at
on the USB drive. Do not copy the RAR archive itself to that path.

Insert the USB drive and choose Settings > System Update > Update via Storage Media. Confirm the displayed update is the intended HFW release. If it is not detected or a same-version install is refused, follow the release’s recovery-mode instructions.

After the firmware installation finishes, open the PS3 Internet Browser and visit the HEN installer linked above. Turn off Confirm Browser Close in the browser Tools settings as directed by the installer.

Choose Initialize HEN installer, then Install HEN when initialization succeeds. Let the installer complete and follow its reboot prompt. Use the official alternate installer instructions if this route fails.
Enable HEN after starting the console
Use Enable HEN under Game on the XMB. Wait for its success notification before launching homebrew. Install compatible PKG apps through the available Package Manager.
Check the project release notes before updating either. The system version display alone does not prove that HFW and HEN installed correctly.

Choose Download .p3t above. On a computer, save the file to Downloads. On a phone, save it in Files or Downloads, then move it to a USB drive using a compatible adaptor or transfer it to a computer first. Keep the .p3t extension; do not rename it to .pkg or .zip.
Use a FAT32 USB storage device your PS3 can read; Sony also lists FAT16 support. Create a folder called
at its root, then a folder called
inside it. Copy the .p3t file into THEME. The themes here are already P3T files and need no extraction.
Connect the storage device, then open
. Choose the storage device and theme. Installation copies the theme to the system storage.
, select the installed theme and choose
. You can now disconnect the removable storage.
Use the exact folder names. A theme inside Downloads or an extra nested folder will not appear in Install.
Find a theme on your phone or PC
Open Download on a PS3 on its card and note the short address. Each one is supplied by Themezer for that exact theme.
Enter the complete short address on PS3
In the PS3 Internet Browser, type the displayed
address. You do not need to load Themezer’s modern main website on the PS3.

Sony says theme downloads through the browser install when the download completes. Follow the console’s prompts, then select the installed theme in Theme Settings and choose Apply. Prompts may vary by firmware.
Use USB if the connection fails
A modern website, certificate or network error may stop an older console browser. Save the P3T on a phone or computer and use the documented USB route above.
Keep a copy; change it whenever you like

Each card shows the P3T download size. Keep enough free system storage for installation; the displayed file size is not a measured installed-space requirement. Your saved USB or phone copy is separate from the installed theme.
To switch back, choose a built-in theme in Theme Settings. To remove an installed theme, select it in the theme list, press the confirm button and choose
, as described in Sony’s manual. Keep your original P3T if you may reinstall later.
Theme Settings is different from XMB modification
These P3T downloads customize theme artwork, icons, sounds or backgrounds. They do not install custom firmware, change firmware files, add a PS4 operating system, or provide a custom XMB loader.
Replacing flash resources, fonts or XMB components is a separate homebrew workflow with its own CFW/HEN and firmware requirements. Do not follow those instructions to install an ordinary P3T.
Check the result on your console

Creators may supply only some icons; Sony notes that missing artwork can keep default icons or use another icon from the theme. Themes with multiple backgrounds may choose one randomly. Preview appearance, sounds and animation can differ with display and brightness settings.

PS4 PS Patch System loader artwork
PS4 ELF engine. Project-confirmed firmware range 9.00–12.52; requires a compatible elfldr listening on 9021. The ELF is not a BIN payload.
Start the compatible PS4 elfldr and explicitly send the Orbis ELF to port 9021. Then open the patch manager on console port 23900; use /data/user/patches/xml_orbis for CUSA XML files.
PS4 console PKG for managing cheats, patches and plugins. Install in your existing compatible homebrew environment; patch application additionally needs the matching GoldHEN plugin engine.
Install the PKG with your supported PS4 package installer. Open PS4 Cheats Manager to enable only the patch matching your exact title ID and game update, then fully restart the game.
PS4 GoldHEN 2.3 or newer on a firmware supported by that GoldHEN release. Original plugin release archive; extract it before selecting a PRX.
The selected game_patch.prx is also provided directly. Preserve existing plugins.ini entries; configure the game-patch plugin for your title ID instead of loading every plugin.
PS4 GoldHEN 2.3 or newer, on a firmware supported by that release. Native PRX plugin; not an ELF payload and not a PS5 plugin.

Place game_patch.prx in /data/GoldHEN/plugins/, merge its line into the matching CUSA title section of /data/GoldHEN/plugins.ini, enable plugin loading in GoldHEN and select the exact XML option in PS4 Cheats Manager. Preserve existing plugin configuration.
