Check downloads and disable automatic updates

Open Notifications → Downloads and check for a pending system-software update. The video removes a queued update before continuing. In Settings → Network, temporarily turn off Connect to the Internet. Then open Settings → System → Automatic Downloads and disable the automatic-download options shown in the tutorial.

Read Settings → System → System Information. This tutorial demonstrates 13.52 and describes the browser route from 7.00 through 13.52. Stay on an already supported version; the optional update video is not a requirement. Use a separate compatible route for older firmware, and the separate guide for 14.00.

Re-enable Connect to the Internet and choose Set Up Internet Connection. Select Wi-Fi or LAN Cable, then Custom. Keep IP settings appropriate for your network, use Do Not Specify for DHCP on a typical setup, and choose Manual DNS. The video supplies 45.56.67.85 with 62.210.38.117 as an alternate primary resolver. Finish with the normal MTU and proxy settings, then test ordinary browsing. Automatic/Easy settings remove this DNS blocking if the resolver prevents a connection.
Clear the browser before the first setup

In Internet Browser, use Options to remove frequently used pages. Open Settings and delete cookies and website data. Clear Browsing History as shown, then close and reopen the browser. Do this during initial setup or documented troubleshooting; clearing website data later can remove the offline cache.
Open and cache the matching host

Open https://speedy-away.github.io/hosts/ps4/ in the PS4 browser and select your exact installed firmware. Choose the compatible browser entry and follow its displayed loading and cache instructions. Bookmark the selected entry if it supports offline use; cache preparation and restart steps depend on that build. This guide page is separate from the exploit host.
Wait for GoldHEN and confirm success

After reopening the cached host, let its compatible jailbreak chain finish. Confirm the GoldHEN notification and settings appear before installing homebrew. A memory error may require dismissing the message and retrying as shown; a failure or system crash may require a restart. Follow the host's current recovery prompts, and do not keep retriggering a host once GoldHEN is already active.

Once caching has completed, the video demonstrates loading the bookmarked page with Connect to the Internet disabled. Keep the cached browser data if you want this offline route. Do not launch the exploit again merely to test the cache while your current GoldHEN session is already running. Reconnect only when a task needs network access.
Configure the GoldHEN features you need

Open GoldHEN settings. Debug Settings contains Package Installer; Cheat Settings and Plugin Settings provide archive updates. The video also shows the FPS overlay, FTP and payload-server settings, local/USB payload loading and date/time synchronization. GoldHEN documents an update-blocking feature, but keep the preparation settings in place instead of treating it as a guarantee against every update or PSN connection.

For the USB method shown, copy the PS4 PKG files to the root of an exFAT or FAT32 USB drive, connect it to the PS4, then open GoldHEN → Debug Settings → Package Installer. Select the intended homebrew package or the documented Install All option. Homebrew Store can then install more supported homebrew on the console. Archives and ELF/BIN payloads need their own loading or extraction steps; they are not USB PKG installs.
Finish patch or plugin setup only when needed

The video demonstrates updating cheats, patches and plugins through GoldHEN, with PS4 Cheats Manager as a fallback if an archive update fails. Match any patch or plugin to the game's title ID and update. Enable the plugin loader and game-patch plugin only after installing the matching components; a downloaded mod file alone is not a completed installation.
Reload the jailbreak after a restart

A full restart ends the active jailbreak session. Installed homebrew and downloaded files remain on storage, but their launch may be restricted until you reopen the bookmarked compatible host and GoldHEN loads again. The video also discusses Rest Mode; its behavior is specific to the exploit and payload build rather than a permanent CFW guarantee.

The video's optional firmware-update companion references GoldHEN 2.4b18.11. The current GamerHack host advertises 2.4b18.12. Hosted payloads can change; the site's retained GoldHEN 2.3 archive is not the build demonstrated for 13.52.
Apps and saved files remain on the HDD/SSD after a restart, but the jailbreak session ends. Reload the compatible browser host after rebooting before starting homebrew.

Manage your game libraries and choose compatibility tools for Windows games.
Install Epic, GOG, and Amazon Prime Games titles. Manage Wine or Proton and add games to Steam for access in Game Mode.
Install community compatibility tools such as GE-Proton. Restart Steam, then select the installed version in a game's Compatibility settings.
Manage non-Steam games and launchers in one library. Install Lutris through Discover in Desktop Mode, then create Steam shortcuts for the games you want in Game Mode.

Install game-specific Windows components inside a Steam game's Proton environment. Use its graphical interface when a game's setup instructions call for particular dependencies, rather than changing every game.
Use the dependencies named by the game's setup guide.

Create separate environments for Windows games and software. Manage runners and dependencies through a graphical interface, then run the installer or program inside its selected bottle in Desktop Mode.
The official supported package is the Flatpak version.
Install GE-Proton and select it for one game
ProtonUp-Qt manages additional compatibility tools. Install a version first, then choose it separately for the game that needs it.
In Desktop Mode, install ProtonUp-Qt from Discover or use the Linux download on its official site.
Open ProtonUp-Qt, select your Steam installation, choose Add version, and select the GE-Proton version you need.
Wait for installation to finish, then fully restart Steam so it can find the new compatibility tool.
Open the game's Properties, select Compatibility, enable the specific compatibility-tool option, and select the installed GE-Proton version.
Compatibility varies by game. Keep a working configuration available and test changes one game at a time.
Choose a launcher for non-Steam Windows games
Choose the workflow that matches your game's source. Heroic, Lutris, and Bottles each manage their own installations and settings.
Use Heroic for your Epic, GOG, or Amazon library. Sign into the relevant service and install a game you own.
Use Lutris for a supported game installer or another collection. Follow that game's installation instructions and test its launcher entry.
Use Bottles for a separate Windows software environment. Create a Gaming bottle and follow the app's installer instructions inside it.
Once the game works in Desktop Mode, use the launcher's Steam shortcut option where available, then test the shortcut in Game Mode.
Pick one suitable workflow for each installation; adding more launchers does not fix an incompatible game.
Fix a Flatpak folder permission or game dependency
Use Flatseal for a specific app's folder access. Use Protontricks only when a game's instructions require a Windows component or prefix change.
Close the affected application, open Flatseal, and select that application's entry rather than changing permissions for every app.
For an inaccessible library folder, add only its required path under Filesystem, Other files. Use read-only access when sufficient.
Restart the affected app and test access. Use Flatseal's Reset button if your permission changes cause problems.
For a documented Protontricks fix, launch the game once through Steam with its selected Proton tool, close it, then select it in Protontricks.
Apply only the components or actions named by the game's instructions, then test the game again.

Original whatwhatboy preview: Steam Deck Plugins & Customization
Install Decky Loader first, then add plugins from its stable store.
Add a plugin menu and community plugin store to Game Mode. Browse customization, artwork, and utility plugins from the Deck's Quick Access menu.
Customize the Steam interface with community CSS themes. Install the plugin through Decky, then choose and manage themes from its menu.
Requires Decky Loader; install through its built-in stable store.
Change library artwork, icons, and game images in Game Mode, including non-Steam shortcuts. Open a game's context menu and choose Change Artwork.
Show tappable ProtonDB community compatibility badges on game pages. Open the reports to compare other players' settings and experiences with a title.
Adjust CPU, GPU, and battery controls with per-game settings. For manual tuning: change one setting at a time and keep defaults available to restore.
Requires Decky Loader. Advanced manual tuning; results depend on the game.
Create, reorder, filter, and hide library tabs in Game Mode. Build a tab for a collection, installed games, or non-Steam titles to make a large library easier to browse.
Requires Decky Loader; install through its stable plugin store.
Display HowLongToBeat completion-time estimates on game pages. Open View Details for the source listing and adjust the information bar from the plugin menu.
Estimates depend on HowLongToBeat data and its availability.
Inspect per-game shader-cache and compatibility-data usage from Game Mode. Identify space usage before considering selective cleanup; compatibility folders can also contain game settings and saves.
Requires Decky Loader. Review data and backups before removing anything.
Reconnect already paired headphones, controllers, and other Bluetooth devices from Quick Access while a game is running.
Pair new devices in Steam Settings first; this plugin is a shortcut to existing pairings.
Pause and resume a running game from Quick Access, or optionally pause it when it loses focus. Useful for switching between applications without closing them.
Paused games keep their RAM and VRAM. Save first and test with an offline game; some games do not resume reliably.
Replace Steam interface sound effects with sound packs from the built-in Pack Manager. Browse packs and try one at a time from Game Mode.
Requires Decky Loader. Sound packs are downloaded separately through the plugin.
Browse and install startup animations, choose an installed animation, or randomize your selection on boot. Manage the selection from Quick Access.
Requires Decky Loader. Animation files are separate downloads; Steam customization settings can affect which movie plays.
Check and install Flatpak app updates without switching to Desktop Mode. Start with manual checks, then choose whether to enable notifications or automatic updates.
Requires root permissions through Decky. Supports system-installed Flatpaks; user-installed apps and extra installation locations are not supported.
Launch desktop applications from the Quick Access menu and add shortcuts to your Steam library. Useful for opening an already installed utility from Game Mode.
Limited maintenance: the author cannot promise fixes. The plugin supports one application at a time; Steam library shortcuts remain an alternative.
Install Decky Loader and your first plugin
Decky adds a plugin menu to Game Mode. Start with its stable release and install plugins through the built-in store.
In Desktop Mode, open Decky's official site, download the installer, and follow its stable-release installation instructions.
Return to Game Mode, press the three-dot Quick Access button, and select the Decky plug tab.
Open the store icon, search for the plugin's exact name, and select Install.
Open the installed plugin from the Decky tab. Check Decky and plugin updates after Steam client changes.
PowerTools is advanced manual tuning, with no guaranteed FPS gain. ProtonDB Badges shows community reports, separate from Valve's Deck Verified rating.
Customize Steam menus and game artwork
Use CSS Loader for interface themes and SteamGridDB for game artwork. Both install through Decky's store in Game Mode.
Open Quick Access, select the Decky plug tab, and open its store. Install CSS Loader and SteamGridDB.
Open CSS Loader from the Decky tab, browse its theme collection, and enable the theme you want to try.
For artwork, open a game's context menu from your library or its settings cog, then choose Change Artwork.
Browse SteamGridDB's images or select a local image. Check the result in your library before changing other games.
Try one interface theme at a time so you can identify and disable it if a Steam update changes the layout.
Organize library tabs and compare game lengths
TabMaster customizes your library tabs. HLTB for Deck adds completion-time estimates to game pages.
Install TabMaster and HLTB for Deck from Decky's stable plugin store in Game Mode.
Open TabMaster in Quick Access. Add or edit a tab, then choose a collection, installed-game, or platform filter for the titles you want to see.
Reorder or hide tabs as needed, then return to the library and check the result.
Open a game page to see its HowLongToBeat estimates. Use View Details to inspect the source listing, and adjust the bar's appearance in the HLTB plugin menu.
Completion times are community estimates. HLTB data can become temporarily unavailable when its upstream service changes.
Inspect disk usage and game caches
Filelight maps folders in Desktop Mode. Storage Cleaner shows per-game cache and compatibility-data usage through Decky.
Install Filelight from Discover in Desktop Mode. Scan your home folder or the drive you want to inspect.
Explore larger segments of the ring map to identify the folders using space. Review their paths and contents before making changes.
For Game Mode inspection, install Storage Cleaner through Decky's stable store, then open it from the Decky tab.
Read the per-game shader-cache and compatibility-data sizes. Leave cleanup actions untouched while you identify the data and check your backups.
Compatibility folders can contain saves and settings. Shader caches may regenerate after removal, so clearing them is not a permanent storage saving.
Reconnect Bluetooth devices from your game
Pair a device once in Steam Settings, then use the Bluetooth plugin as a Quick Access shortcut.
Open Steam Settings, select Bluetooth, enable it, and pair your headphones or controller using the normal Steam interface.
Open Quick Access with the three-dot button, select Decky, and install Bluetooth from its stable plugin store.
Open Bluetooth in the Decky tab and select your already paired device to reconnect it.
Check that the controller or headphones work in your game. If the device is missing, return to Steam Settings and confirm its pairing.
The plugin connects existing pairings; it does not replace initial device pairing in Steam Settings.
Pause and resume an offline game
Use manual pause first so you can check how a game behaves before enabling focus-based automation.
Install Pause Games from the stable Decky store, launch an offline game, and save your progress.
Open Quick Access, select Decky, then open Pause Games to see its running-game list.
Select the game icon with the pause symbol to stop it. Select its play symbol to resume, then check controls and audio.
If manual pausing works, optionally enable Pause on focus loss. Test switching apps and turn the option off if the game freezes or loses input.
This stops running processes; it does not save their state to disk or release their RAM/VRAM. Network sessions may time out while paused. Save frequently.
Install a Steam menu sound pack
Audio Loader uses a curated Pack Manager to install sound packs for the Steam interface.
Install Audio Loader from the stable Decky store, then open it from the Decky tab in Quick Access.
While connected to the internet, open the plugin's Pack Manager and browse the available sound packs.
Install a pack and select it in Audio Loader. Navigate the Steam menus to check its sound effects.
Try one pack at a time. Return to Audio Loader to disable or change the selected pack if you want different menu sounds.
Menu sound packs are separate from game audio. Use the plugin manager rather than manually copying theme folders.
Animation Changer manages installed startup animations and can choose a different one each boot.
Install Animation Changer from Decky's stable plugin store and open it from Quick Access.
Open its animation browser, choose a startup animation from SteamDeckRepo, and install it.
Select the installed animation in the plugin. Check Steam Settings > Customization if a different Startup Movie overrides it; follow the project's current setting instructions.
Restart the Deck when convenient to check the result. Enable randomization only if you want to rotate through your installed animations.
The built-in browser supplies startup animations. Suspend-animation configuration is a separate advanced feature described by the project.
Check Flatpak app updates in Game Mode
Start with manual update checks before deciding whether you want background automation.
Install AutoFlatpaks from Decky's stable plugin store and open it from Quick Access.
Keep automatic upgrading disabled initially. Run a manual check for available Flatpak updates.
Open the package manager to review the apps and runtimes. Select the updates you want, start the queue, and keep the Deck awake until it finishes.
Choose a check interval and notification style if useful. Enable upgrading without user interaction only if you want automatic updates.
The plugin requires root permissions and currently supports system-installed Flatpaks only. It updates Flatpak apps and runtimes, not SteamOS or Steam games.
Open an installed desktop app from Quick Access
Quick Launch opens installed apps in Game Mode and can create Steam library shortcuts.
Install the desktop application you need in Desktop Mode and check its normal setup first.
Return to Game Mode and install Quick Launch from the stable Decky plugin store.
Open Quick Launch from Decky's Quick Access tab, choose an installed app, and launch it.
Close that application before opening another through the plugin. Use the plugin's shortcut action if you also want the app listed in your Steam library.
The author reports limited maintenance and support for one application at a time. If it stops working after a Steam update, add the application to Steam from Desktop Mode instead.

Play games running on a PC or PlayStation console. The host device is required.
Stream games from your gaming PC. Set up Sunshine on the host, pair Moonlight, and use a reliable network for responsive remote play.
Stream from your PS4 or PS5 to the Deck. Enable Remote Play on the console, then follow the registration guide to pair the app.
Pair Moonlight with a gaming PC
Moonlight receives the stream on your Deck. Sunshine runs on the gaming PC that renders and launches the games.
Install Sunshine on the host PC using its official instructions, start it, and complete the initial configuration.
Install Moonlight on the Deck and connect both devices to the same local network for the first pairing.
Open Moonlight and select the PC. If it is not discovered, add the PC's local IP address manually.
Enter the PIN shown by Moonlight in Sunshine's PIN page on the host, then select a game or application to test.
Keep the host PC running while streaming. Confirm local play works before following the projects' separate remote-network instructions.
Register a PS4 or PS5 with chiaki-ng
Set up your own PlayStation console first, then register chiaki-ng. Start with the Deck and console on the same home network.
Enable Remote Play in your console's settings. Use the official configuration guide for the different PS4 and PS5 menu paths.
Install and open chiaki-ng in Desktop Mode. Keep the console powered on and select it when it is discovered.
Follow chiaki-ng's PSN account and registration guide. Use its automatic registration flow or the documented console-link PIN method.
Confirm the console is marked registered, then open it and test a game locally before configuring optional rest-mode wake or remote access.
Use the guide matching your console and chosen registration method; account registration and console pairing are separate setup steps.

In desktop Steam, choose Games > Add a Non-Steam Game to My Library. Find the app under Non-Steam in Game Mode.
Choose a walkthrough. Each guide links to the project's own instructions.
Move files between your Deck and another device
LocalSend transfers files over your local network. Install it on both devices and keep its receive window available on the destination.
Install LocalSend on the Deck in Desktop Mode and on the phone or computer holding your files.
Connect both devices to the same local network and open LocalSend on each device so they can discover one another.
On the sending device, choose the files, select Send, and pick the receiving device's displayed name.
Confirm the incoming transfer on the receiving device. Wait for completion, then open its receive folder and check the files.
If discovery fails, check the project's network troubleshooting instructions. A guest Wi-Fi network may separate connected devices.
Sync a selected folder with Syncthing
Set up a shared folder between your own devices. Start with a small test folder before choosing a game-save or document folder.
In Desktop Mode, unpack the official Linux AMD64 build and start its syncthing executable following the project guide. Start Syncthing on your other device too.
Open the local browser interface shown by Syncthing. Add the other device using its device ID, and accept the matching device on that device.
Add a folder with the path you want to share. Select the paired device, then accept the shared folder and choose its destination on the receiving device.
Copy a test file into the shared folder and wait for both devices to report that they are up to date. Keep Syncthing running while you need synchronization.
Sync propagates edits and deletions. Keep independent save backups; optional versioning archives incoming changes and is configured separately on each device.
Inspect and extract an archive with PeaZip
Use Desktop Mode to browse a download before extracting it into a chosen folder.
Unpack the official portable Linux Qt6 build and open PeaZip from the extracted application folder, following its Linux setup notes.
Open the archive in PeaZip and review the file list. For a multipart archive, keep all supplied parts together.
Choose Extract, select a new destination folder, and review the overwrite and output options. Keep deletion of the original archive disabled.
Complete extraction and check the output folder in Dolphin. Keep the original archive and use the extracted files only as directed by their project.
. GE-Proton is optional and does not make every Windows game compatible.
EmuDeck and RetroDECK are alternative setups. Steam ROM Manager organizes shortcuts and artwork. Games and required BIOS files are supplied separately.
Check Decky and plugin compatibility after SteamOS or Steam client updates. Use stable releases and each project's troubleshooting guide when something changes.

Open the Aroma plugin menu with L + D-pad Down + Minus. Check Inkay’s Connect to Pretendo Network setting, restart into Aroma, then recheck the official service status. Retain the full WPS/WMS pair.
Your PNID is separate from your NNID. Use the official account guidance and back up saves before any account/save transfer. Keep passwords and console-specific dumps private.

Use the maintained vWii-specific guide. Wii U WUHB apps go under /wiiu/apps/; vWii Homebrew Channel apps use /apps/
/boot.dol at the SD root. The same card can hold both trees. Keep a NAND backup. BootMii cannot be installed on vWii; do not substitute ordinary Wii system files, IOS packages or themes.
Install and maintain the Wii environment
With Aroma and the required backups prepared, use the guide’s Compat Title Installer Aroma build. It installs the vWii Homebrew Channel; it is not a native Wii U game launcher.
Use a compatible Wii Remote and the peripherals required by each app. Back up the SD card before changes. Keep the entire app folder, including meta.xml, icon.png and runtime data.
Use the guide’s model-specific Priiloader and cIOS instructions when the task needs them. An emulator or Homebrew Channel app does not automatically require cIOS. Avoid old Wii-only installers.
Keep evWii on the Wii U side
The archived evWii WPS controls vWii display/power behavior from Aroma. Its documented limitations still apply; it is not installed inside the vWii Homebrew Channel.

Close the app, back up its documented save/profile directories, then select the app in Device Portal’s Apps manager and use Remove / Uninstall. Preserve your external game and save folders. Reinstalling a different package identity does not automatically migrate old data.

Why do I have to disable my antivirus?

Game cheats use code injection techniques that look similar to malware, so antivirus programs flag them even though they are harmless. This is called a "false positive." You can either temporarily disable real-time protection or add an exclusion folder. Always download only from trusted sources and scan files on VirusTotal if you are unsure.
Are the cheats safe to use?

Modding always carries some risk. We curate and test everything we share to minimize issues, but no cheat is 100% undetectable forever. Game updates and new anti-cheat patches can change detection status at any time. Use cheats responsibly and check our Safety page for best practices before you start.

Most cheats and tools are built with C# and require the .NET runtime to function. Without it you will see errors like ".NET Framework is not installed." Install the version your tool needs -- .NET 4.8 covers legacy apps while .NET 6 and .NET 8 cover modern ones.

C++ based tools and game mods need Visual C++ runtime libraries. Missing them causes "VCRUNTIME140.dll was not found" and similar DLL errors. The all-in-one package installs every version from 2005 to 2022 in one step.

Important safety information for using gaming tools
Follow these guidelines to stay safe while modding
Keep your antivirus software updated at all times. Scan every file before running it on your system. Use tools like VirusTotal to verify downloads from multiple engines.
Always use alternative accounts for modding and cheating. Never risk your main account. Create dedicated alt accounts specifically for testing modifications.
Only download from trusted and verified sources. Avoid random links, suspicious websites, and unverified third-party downloads. Stick to known communities.
Always use the latest versions of cheats and mods. Outdated tools are more likely to be detected and may contain unpatched security vulnerabilities.
Follow installation guides carefully and completely. Skipping steps can lead to crashes, bans, or security issues. Read all documentation before proceeding.
Always create backups before installing any mods or cheats. Back up game files, save data, and create system restore points so you can recover if something goes wrong.
Understanding why gaming tools trigger security warnings

Cheat software uses injection techniques similar to malware, such as DLL injection and memory modification. This causes antivirus programs to flag them as threats, even when they are legitimate tools from trusted sources.

Add the cheat folder to your antivirus exclusion list before extracting files. In Windows Defender, go to Settings > Virus & Threat Protection > Exclusions and add the folder path. This prevents automatic deletion of legitimate tools.

Upload suspicious files to VirusTotal.com to scan with multiple engines. A few detections among many clean results typically indicates a false positive. If the majority flag it, avoid the file entirely.

Extract the complete Windows release and configure your own supported Xbox game dump. For Linux, follow the project’s Wine dependencies and known-version caveats; do not treat it as a normal native Linux package.
Check its compatibility list and Wine caveats for the selected title. It is a separate approach from xemu’s full-system setup.

Install a desktop package for your OS, then obtain the intended core. A RetroArch source-only archive is not an installed frontend, and an emulator core is not the whole application.

Install or extract the complete desktop package. Set the System/BIOS, savefile and save-state directories under Settings > Directory, install the chosen core, then use Load Content with your own files.
Core support, required firmware and save-state behaviour vary by emulated system. Check the selected core’s documentation.
A dedicated Linux-based RetroArch distribution installed on supported PC or single-board hardware.
Choose your exact hardware image on the publisher’s site.
A hardware-matched image and the separate storage/install procedure. The Windows/macOS/Linux choices on its website refer to the computer used to prepare media, not three desktop application builds.

Use the official hardware selector and installation tutorial. Keep existing data backed up and choose the intended boot/storage device. This catalogue links the publisher’s images without downloading every hardware variant.
Listed separately from desktop apps because it supplies an operating-system image.
A dedicated emulation system with hardware-specific PC and single-board-computer images.
Choose the exact target hardware from the publisher’s download page. This is not a Windows or macOS desktop app, even when those systems prepare the install media.
Follow the official target-hardware installation route and preserve existing storage data before preparing boot media. Add your own supported content after setup.

Extract the complete package, run its setup wizard, choose your BIOS directory and add your own disc dumps. Keep multi-track BIN/CUE files together; select the cue sheet where appropriate.
Use default compatibility settings first. The latest tag is rolling, so archived checksums identify the exact file captured.

Download the intended OS package from the official page. Keep its required files together, configure BIOS and controller settings, and open your own supported disc dump. Do not assume the Windows version number applies to Linux or macOS.
